# Strategic Research Framework

### 1. Core Objective & Business Context

- **Business problem:** LearnSphere needs to understand why learners do not sustain engagement or complete courses, and which parts of the learning experience most influence continued progress.
- **Research scope:** The study will examine content relevance, learning formats, adaptive tools, progress feedback, social learning, gamification, and the experience of current, former, potential, and decision-influencing stakeholders.
- **Why this matters now:** The research has been triggered by learner complaints, low engagement or completion, upcoming feature planning, competitive pressure, and possible expansion into certifications or institutional partnerships. These pressures require LearnSphere to distinguish genuine experience problems from unmet expectations or differences between learner groups.
- **What knowing the answer enables:** LearnSphere will be able to identify the strongest barriers to course completion, separate issues affecting current learners from reasons for inactivity or non-adoption, and prioritize product improvements that are most likely to increase sustained engagement.
- **Important stakeholder distinction:** Learners should provide the primary experience and completion evidence. Parents or guardians, teachers, and academic administrators should be routed to separate role-appropriate modules rather than being combined into a single learner satisfaction score.

### 2. Secondary Research Snapshot

- **Digital learning engagement requires more than platform access:** The OECD identifies engagement as a central challenge in digital learning and highlights the need to measure engagement and design interventions when disengagement begins. This supports measuring specific drop-off moments, not only overall satisfaction. — OECD Digital Education Outlook ([oecd.org](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-digital-education-outlook-2021_589b283f-en/full-report/component-7.html))
- **India has a large and increasingly structured digital-learning ecosystem:** The Government of India’s PM e-VIDYA initiative brings together multiple digital and online education channels and is designed to benefit nearly 25 crore school-going children. LearnSphere should therefore benchmark against both commercial platforms and public or institution-linked learning alternatives. — Ministry of Education, Government of India ([pmevidya.education.gov.in](https://pmevidya.education.gov.in/))
- **Institutional and educator use is strategically relevant:** DIKSHA operates across 35 states and union territories and provides large volumes of curriculum-linked digital content, showing why teacher, administrator, curriculum alignment, and partnership expectations may become important for LearnSphere’s expansion plans. — Press Information Bureau, Government of India ([dsel.education.gov.in](http://dsel.education.gov.in/sites/default/files/update/PIB2036640.pdf))
- **AI and personalized support are becoming important parts of online learning value propositions:** Coursera’s 2025 learner-outcomes research reports that 94% of full-time professionals who completed GenAI content reported a positive impact at work, while 94% of users of its AI coaching feature said it improved their learning experience. These are provider-sponsored findings, so LearnSphere should test whether its own AI tools create measurable engagement value rather than assuming that AI is inherently motivating. — Coursera and The Harris Poll ([coursera.org](https://www.coursera.org/enterprise/resources/ebook/learner-outcomes), [assets.ctfassets.net](https://assets.ctfassets.net/00atxywtfxvd/2eocGVEBKQlIHuLNaSuK1l/18f31949bff069d78a22daf8869566b7/2025-coursera-learner-outcomes-report.pdf))
- **Competitive pressure is likely to come from several directions:** LearnSphere may compete not only with direct online-learning platforms but also with public digital resources, institutional learning systems, creator-led content, coaching platforms, and informal peer-learning communities. The survey should therefore measure alternatives used and the specific reasons users switch or divide their learning time.

### 3. Research Type & Methodology

- **Study type:** Mixed-method **Customer Experience / Learner Experience**, **Usage & Attitude**, and **Feature or Experience Prioritization** research.
- **Stimulus count:** The current brief contains zero discrete stimuli to show. The listed areas are experience domains, not specific concepts, screens, feature designs, or competing assets. Therefore, cell-based designs such as monadic, sequential monadic, A/B, or paired comparison do not apply at this stage.
- **Research design:** A linear, modular questionnaire with role-based routing and a general-to-specific funnel.
- **Why this approach:** The main decision is how to improve learner engagement and course completion, which requires behavioral evidence, journey diagnosis, satisfaction drivers, and barriers rather than a simple preference test. A modular design will allow current learners, inactive learners, potential users, parents, and educators to answer only the sections relevant to their relationship with LearnSphere.
- **Feature-prioritization overlay:** If LearnSphere provides a defined list of at least five candidate features or improvements, a MaxDiff exercise should be added to produce a clearer preference hierarchy. This should be treated as a prioritization module, not as a stimulus-cell test.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Pure monadic testing:** Not selected because no discrete concepts, designs, or feature prototypes are currently specified.
  - **Sequential monadic testing:** Not selected because respondents are not being asked to evaluate multiple independent assets.
  - **Conjoint or choice-based conjoint:** Not selected because the current decision concerns experience improvement and completion barriers, not quantified trade-offs between product configurations and prices.
  - **Standalone NPS or CSAT survey:** Not selected because a single score would not explain the behavioral causes of disengagement, inactivity, or incomplete courses.
- **User control:** If you prefer a different methodology, such as adding a MaxDiff feature-prioritization exercise or testing specific product prototypes, the design can be switched before the research brief is generated.
- **Survey design logic:** Begin with recent behavior and usage context, then measure the learning journey, followed by satisfaction and engagement drivers. Ask unaided barriers and reasons before presenting structured response options where possible. Current and former learners should receive different paths; potential users should not be asked to rate experiences they have not had. Parents, teachers, and administrators should receive role-specific questions about influence, learning outcomes, implementation, and support needs.
- **Quality controls:** Use platform attention checks, speeder detection, straight-line detection, minimum completion-time rules, and open-ended gibberish screening. Long or complex batteries should be split across short mobile-friendly screens, with answer options randomized where order effects are not meaningful.
- **Fielding context:** The survey will be deployed to verified Indian respondents through the SuperJ mobile application and web. Age, gender, city, and NCCS targeting should be enforced by the audience system rather than recollected in the questionnaire. Routing, randomization, quotas, attention checks, and media support are available if later product or interface assets are added.

### 4. Target Audience Profile

- **Current LearnSphere students:** Active learners with recent platform experience who can evaluate content quality, learning formats, feedback, adaptive tools, social learning, and the moments that support or interrupt progress.
- **Former or inactive LearnSphere students:** People who have stopped using LearnSphere or failed to complete a course. They are essential for identifying disengagement triggers, unmet expectations, friction points, competing alternatives, and realistic win-back opportunities.
- **Potential users:** People who fit the intended learning need but do not currently use LearnSphere. They can reveal awareness, category expectations, perceived barriers, competing solutions, and what proof would be needed to try the platform.
- **Parents or guardians:** Individuals who influence learning decisions, particularly where the learner is a minor or where household approval, payment, trust, safety, or academic credibility affects adoption.
- **Teachers, instructors, and academic administrators:** Stakeholders who can assess curriculum fit, teaching usefulness, learner monitoring, feedback quality, institutional integration, and partnership readiness.
- **Why these groups matter:** Engagement and completion are not shaped only by the learner interface. Trust, course relevance, instructional quality, feedback, household influence, and institutional support may all affect sustained use.
- **Must-have screening criteria:** Confirm respondent role, familiarity with LearnSphere, current or past usage, recent course or learning activity where applicable, involvement in learning decisions, and whether the respondent has enough experience to answer the relevant module.
- **Reporting principle:** Results should be reported separately by stakeholder role and LearnSphere relationship. Combining all groups into one overall average would risk masking the reasons different groups support, reject, or abandon the platform.

### 5. Key Information Areas & Data Architecture

- **Engagement and completion behavior:** Capture recent login or learning frequency, course-start behavior, lesson completion, quiz participation, progress consistency, and where applicable the point at which learning stopped. → Reveals the difference between stated engagement and actual learning behavior. → Drives targeted retention and completion interventions.
- **Learning journey friction:** Measure difficulty finding the right course, onboarding clarity, navigation, lesson length, technical interruptions, scheduling barriers, and resuming unfinished learning. → Identifies operational friction that may be mistaken for low motivation. → Drives journey and interface improvements.
- **Content quality and course relevance:** Assess relevance to learner goals, clarity, depth, difficulty, curriculum fit, instructor quality, and perceived usefulness. → Shows whether learners disengage because the content does not deliver enough value. → Drives curriculum refresh, course design, and content investment.
- **Learning format effectiveness:** Compare perceived usefulness of video lectures, quizzes, learning plans, practice activities, and other instructional formats using behavioral and outcome-oriented questions. → Identifies which formats support understanding and continued progress. → Drives learning-design priorities rather than popularity-led feature decisions.
- **Adaptive learning, feedback, and progress visibility:** Measure whether AI recommendations, personalized paths, real-time feedback, reminders, dashboards, and progress tracking are noticed, understood, trusted, and acted upon. → Separates feature awareness from genuine behavioral impact. → Drives improvements to personalization, feedback timing, transparency, and motivation loops.
- **Social learning and gamification:** Assess the role of peer interaction, instructor access, discussion, badges, streaks, points, challenges, and recognition. → Reveals which engagement mechanisms create meaningful learning momentum versus superficial activity. → Drives community and gamification design decisions.
- **Reasons for inactivity and alternatives:** Capture primary and secondary reasons for stopping or not starting, competing platforms or offline options used, and what would make the respondent return or try LearnSphere. → Reveals churn triggers, switching dynamics, and unmet expectations. → Drives retention, win-back, positioning, and acquisition strategy.
- **Feature and improvement prioritization:** If a defined list is supplied, use MaxDiff or a structured forced trade-off to prioritize improvements such as better content relevance, shorter lessons, stronger feedback, improved AI recommendations, peer interaction, certifications, or institutional tools. → Produces a relative priority hierarchy instead of inflated ratings across every feature. → Drives the next product-release roadmap.

### 6. Survey Flow & Question Design Approach

- **Phase 1 — Warm-up and screening:** Approximately 2-3 questions covering respondent role, LearnSphere familiarity, current or past usage, and recent learning activity. This establishes credibility before asking detailed evaluations.
- **Phase 2 — Learning context and goals:** Approximately 3-4 questions covering learning objective, course type, expected outcome, study frequency, and the role of parents, teachers, or administrators where relevant. This provides the context needed to interpret completion behavior.
- **Phase 3 — Current experience and journey:** Approximately 5-7 questions covering discovery, onboarding, course selection, content relevance, lesson experience, quizzes, learning plans, navigation, technical friction, and resuming interrupted learning. Current learners should answer the full path; former learners should be routed toward the point of drop-off.
- **Phase 4 — Engagement and completion drivers:** Approximately 5-7 questions covering motivation, progress visibility, feedback, adaptive learning, social learning, gamification, instructor support, workload, confidence, and perceived learning progress. Behavioral anchors should be used so respondents identify what actually happened rather than simply agreeing that a feature sounds useful.
- **Phase 5 — Stakeholder-specific modules:**
  - **Potential users:** Awareness, alternatives, expectations, perceived barriers, trust, and trial requirements.
  - **Parents or guardians:** Influence on choice, trust, safety, value, payment, academic credibility, and evidence of learner progress.
  - **Teachers or administrators:** Curriculum fit, monitoring, feedback, teacher workload, implementation requirements, data visibility, and institutional partnership needs.
- **Phase 6 — Improvement priorities and close:** Approximately 3-5 questions covering the single most important improvement, return or recommendation likelihood, open-ended reasons, and—if supplied—MaxDiff prioritization of candidate features. Close with an action-oriented improvement question rather than only a general satisfaction score.
- **Question design principles:** Use fully labelled 5-point unipolar scales where possible, avoid long agree/disagree grids, keep screens short for mobile completion, randomize non-ordered attribute lists, and use forced-choice or behavioral questions to validate positive claims.
- **Estimated length:** Approximately 18-25 questions for the main learner path, with shorter role-specific paths where possible. Target completion time is 8-12 minutes; modules should be cut rather than allowing the survey to become burdensome.

### 7. Expected Insights & Business Decisions Enabled

- **You will be able to:** Identify the strongest behavioral and experience-level predictors of course engagement and completion.
- **You will be able to:** Quantify where current learners experience friction across onboarding, course discovery, lessons, quizzes, progress tracking, feedback, and resuming unfinished learning.
- **You will be able to:** Diagnose why former or inactive learners stopped using LearnSphere and distinguish product friction from content, motivation, scheduling, trust, or competitive reasons.
- **You will be able to:** Compare the needs of current learners, former learners, potential users, parents or guardians, and educators without blending incompatible perspectives.
- **You will be able to:** Determine whether AI-powered learning tools, progress tracking, social learning, and gamification are noticed, trusted, valued, and linked to continued use.
- **You will be able to:** Build an evidence-based priority list for the next product release, using MaxDiff if a defined set of candidate improvements is supplied.
- **You will be able to decide:** Which learner-experience problems should receive priority to improve engagement and course completion.

# Research Brief: LearnSphere Learner Engagement and Completion Study

### **Background & Context**
LearnSphere needs to understand why learners do not sustain engagement or complete courses, and which parts of the learning experience most influence continued progress. The research is triggered by learner complaints, low engagement or completion, upcoming feature planning, competitive pressure, and possible expansion into certifications or institutional partnerships.

India’s digital-learning environment includes both commercial platforms and large public digital-learning systems. PM e-VIDYA is designed to provide multi-mode digital and online education access to nearly 25 crore school-going children, according to the Government of India. ([pmevidya.education.gov.in](https://pmevidya.education.gov.in/)) DIKSHA also demonstrates the scale and institutional relevance of curriculum-linked digital learning, with extensive state, union-territory, teacher, and learner participation, according to the Government of India’s DIKSHA platform and parliamentary reporting. ([diksha.gov.in](https://diksha.gov.in/), [sansad.in](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/269/AU1162_Lt3Hxb.pdf?source=pqars))

This means LearnSphere must distinguish genuine product-experience problems from content relevance, motivation, scheduling, trust, technical friction, and competition. The study will fill the knowledge gap between overall satisfaction scores and the specific behavioural moments that cause learners to continue, pause, abandon, return, or switch platforms.

---

### **Research Objectives**
Based on the approved strategic framework, this study will address the following objectives.

**Strategic Objectives:**

1. **Identify** the strongest behavioural and experience-level drivers of learner engagement and course completion in order to prioritise improvements that can increase sustained progress.
2. **Diagnose** the causes of inactivity and incomplete courses in order to separate product friction from content, motivation, scheduling, trust, value, and competitive barriers.
3. **Determine** whether LearnSphere’s learning formats, adaptive tools, feedback systems, social-learning elements, and gamification mechanisms create meaningful learning momentum.
4. **Compare** the needs of current learners, former or inactive learners, potential users, parents or guardians, teachers, and academic administrators in order to prevent incompatible perspectives from being combined into one score.
5. **Prioritise** the product improvements most likely to increase engagement, completion, return usage, and recommendation.
6. **Assess** the evidence and capabilities LearnSphere must strengthen before expanding into certifications or institutional partnerships.

**Tactical Objectives:**

1. **Measure** recent learning frequency, course starts, lesson completion, quiz participation, progress consistency, and the point at which learning stopped.
2. **Map** the learning journey from discovery and onboarding through course selection, lesson participation, progress tracking, interruption, and resumption.
3. **Identify** whether content relevance, clarity, difficulty, depth, curriculum fit, instructor quality, or perceived usefulness are linked to disengagement.
4. **Assess** the perceived usefulness of videos, quizzes, practice activities, learning plans, dashboards, reminders, and other instructional formats.
5. **Determine** whether AI recommendations, adaptive learning, real-time feedback, reminders, and progress dashboards are noticed, understood, trusted, and acted upon.
6. **Measure** the contribution of peer interaction, instructor access, discussion, badges, streaks, points, challenges, and recognition to continued learning.
7. **Identify** the primary and secondary reasons learners stop using LearnSphere, fail to complete courses, or decide not to begin.
8. **Map** competing platforms, offline alternatives, creator-led content, coaching services, institutional systems, and informal peer-learning communities used by respondents.
9. **Quantify** the likelihood of continuing, returning, recommending, or trying LearnSphere among relevant respondent groups.
10. **Prioritise** candidate improvements using MaxDiff if LearnSphere supplies a defined list of at least five feature or experience options.
11. **Assess** switching costs, win-back potential, and the interventions most likely to bring inactive learners back.
12. **Determine** the evidence parents, teachers, and administrators require regarding trust, safety, learning outcomes, monitoring, curriculum fit, implementation, and institutional support.

---

### **Type of Study**
We will conduct a **Mixed Methodology study combining Usage & Attitude, Customer Experience / Learner Experience, Churn / Exit, and Feature Prioritization research**.

This combination fits LearnSphere because the business decision is not limited to measuring satisfaction or testing one new feature. LearnSphere needs behavioural evidence, experience diagnosis, lifecycle comparison, stakeholder-specific insight, and a prioritised improvement roadmap. The study will therefore measure what respondents did, where the learning journey breaks down, why engagement stops, and which improvements have the greatest relative value.

---

### **Survey Design Approach**
The selected design is a **linear modular questionnaire with role-based routing and a general-to-specific funnel**. The study currently contains **zero discrete stimuli**: content relevance, adaptive learning, feedback, social learning, and gamification are experience domains rather than defined screens, prototypes, concepts, or competing assets. Under the methodology decision framework, cell-based designs are therefore not appropriate at this stage.

The questionnaire will begin with recent behaviour and usage context, then diagnose the learning journey, followed by satisfaction and engagement drivers, stakeholder-specific modules, and improvement priorities. Current learners will receive the full experience path. Former or inactive learners will be routed toward their last active stage and drop-off reasons. Potential users will answer awareness, expectations, alternatives, and trial-barrier questions rather than rating experiences they have not had. Parents, teachers, and administrators will receive role-appropriate modules.

If LearnSphere provides five or more clearly defined candidate improvements, a **MaxDiff / Best-Worst Scaling** exercise should be added to create a relative priority hierarchy. MaxDiff is preferred to a long rating grid because it forces trade-offs and reduces the risk that respondents rate every feature as important.

**Alternatives considered:**

- **Sequential Monadic:** Not chosen because there are no two to four discrete concepts, prototypes, or product variants for respondents to evaluate independently.
- **Pure Monadic or Proto-Monadic:** Not chosen because the current decision is about diagnosing experience and behaviour, not comparing isolated stimuli across cells.
- **Conjoint / Choice-Based Conjoint:** Not chosen because LearnSphere is not yet asking respondents to trade off defined product configurations, attribute levels, and prices.
- **Standalone CSAT or NPS:** Not chosen because a single satisfaction or advocacy score would not explain completion barriers, churn triggers, or feature priorities.
- **Kano Model:** Not selected for the initial design because the feature list is not yet defined; it may be considered later for roadmap classification into must-have, performance, and delight features.

**Survey Routing Logic:**

- **Skip Logic:** Irrelevant questions will be bypassed based on LearnSphere familiarity, usage status, stakeholder role, and recent activity.
- **Branching:** Current learners, former learners, potential users, parents or guardians, teachers, and administrators will follow separate relevant modules.
- **Display Logic:** Follow-up questions will appear only when a respondent has the relevant experience or selected the relevant activity.
- **Termination Logic:** Respondents without sufficient LearnSphere familiarity or relevant learning experience will be screened out gracefully.
- **Filter Logic:** Follow-ups may focus on platforms, features, or barriers previously selected by the respondent.

**Quality Controls:** Attention checks will be embedded at approximately a 1:9 ratio, with speedster detection below 40-50% of median completion time, straight-line detection across rating batteries, open-ended gibberish screening, and randomisation of non-ordered lists. The survey will use short mobile-friendly screens and avoid long agree/disagree grids.

You can request a different methodology before generating the survey.

---

### **Question Flow & Survey Phases**

- **Phase 1 — Warm-Up and Screening:** Establish respondent role, LearnSphere familiarity, current or past usage, and recent learning activity. This confirms eligibility and routes respondents to the correct module.
- **Phase 2 — Learning Context and Goals:** Capture learning objective, course type, expected outcome, study frequency, and the role of parents, teachers, or administrators where relevant. This provides context for interpreting completion and engagement.
- **Phase 3 — Usage and Completion Behaviour:** Measure recent login or learning frequency, course starts, lesson completion, quiz participation, progress consistency, and the point at which learning stopped. This separates reported attitudes from observed behaviour.
- **Phase 4 — Learning Journey and Experience Diagnosis:** Assess discovery, onboarding, course selection, navigation, lesson length, technical interruptions, scheduling friction, content relevance, curriculum fit, instructor quality, and resumption of unfinished learning.
- **Phase 5 — Engagement Drivers and Learning Support:** Examine motivation, progress visibility, feedback, adaptive learning, AI recommendations, reminders, instructor support, social learning, gamification, workload, confidence, and perceived learning progress.
- **Phase 6 — Role-Specific Modules:** Route potential users to awareness and trial barriers; former learners to churn and win-back questions; parents or guardians to trust, safety, payment, and progress evidence; teachers and administrators to curriculum fit, monitoring, workload, feedback, implementation, and partnership needs.
- **Phase 7 — Improvement Priorities and Close:** Capture the most important improvement, likelihood to continue or return, likelihood to recommend, open-ended suggestions, and MaxDiff prioritisation if a defined feature list is supplied.

The expected main learner path is approximately 18-25 questions and 8-12 minutes. Role-specific paths will be shorter where possible. Break screens may be inserted between major phases if the final questionnaire becomes lengthy.

---

### **Key Data Points to Measure**

**Primary Metrics:**

- **Active-learning frequency** - enables segmentation by engagement intensity and comparison of light, moderate, and heavy learners.
- **Course-start-to-completion behaviour** - identifies where learners progress, pause, or abandon courses.
- **Completion barriers** - quantifies the relative contribution of content, time, motivation, technology, navigation, value, trust, and competing alternatives.
- **Content relevance** - tests the hypothesis that learners who see strong relevance to their goals are more likely to continue and complete courses.
- **Learning-journey satisfaction** - identifies the stages of discovery, onboarding, navigation, lesson use, quizzes, and resumption that require improvement.
- **Perceived learning progress** - measures whether respondents believe LearnSphere is helping them achieve their intended outcome.
- **Feedback usefulness and timeliness** - tests whether feedback reduces uncertainty and supports continued progress.
- **Adaptive-tool awareness, usefulness, and trust** - separates exposure to AI or personalised tools from actual behavioural value.
- **Social-learning value** - measures the contribution of peers, discussions, instructor access, and community support.
- **Gamification contribution** - determines whether streaks, points, badges, challenges, and recognition create meaningful momentum or only superficial activity.
- **Likelihood to continue** - provides a forward-looking retention indicator for current learners.
- **Likelihood to return** - measures win-back potential among former or inactive learners.
- **Likelihood to recommend and NPS** - provides an advocacy benchmark alongside diagnostic reason probes.
- **Primary churn reason** - identifies the single most influential trigger for inactivity or abandonment.
- **Alternative-platform usage** - maps competitive and offline substitutes that divide learning time.
- **Feature priority utility** - produces a relative improvement hierarchy through MaxDiff when five or more candidate improvements are supplied.

**Supporting Metrics:**

- Learning objective and expected outcome - provides context for differences in engagement and completion.
- Course type and subject area - allows comparison of needs across learning missions.
- Frequency of quizzes and practice - helps determine whether active practice is associated with sustained progress.
- Lesson-length preference and scheduling constraints - distinguishes motivation barriers from time and workload friction.
- Course discovery and selection difficulty - identifies acquisition and onboarding issues.
- Technical interruptions and device or connectivity friction - separates operational barriers from content dissatisfaction.
- Trust in recommendations and progress dashboards - provides context for adoption of personalised tools.
- Parent or guardian influence - measures household approval, payment, safety, credibility, and progress-monitoring requirements.
- Teacher and administrator expectations - assesses curriculum fit, implementation readiness, data visibility, and institutional support needs.
- Awareness and consideration among potential users - identifies acquisition and positioning gaps.
- Return or trial requirements - identifies the proof points needed to restart or begin using LearnSphere.

**Advanced Analytics We’ll Apply:**

- **Cross-tabulation and significance testing** to compare current, former, potential, parent or guardian, teacher, and administrator groups.
- **Driver analysis** to identify which experience factors most strongly relate to continuation, completion, return, and recommendation.
- **Journey-stage gap analysis** to compare expected and experienced performance across discovery, onboarding, learning, feedback, and resumption.
- **Churn segmentation** to distinguish content-led, time-led, motivation-led, technology-led, value-led, and competition-led inactivity.
- **MaxDiff preference shares** to rank candidate feature or experience improvements when a defined item list is available.
- **Open-ended thematic and sentiment analysis** to identify recurring emotional and functional barriers.
- **Lifecycle comparison** to identify differences between current learners, former learners, and potential users.
- **Stakeholder role comparison** to prevent learner, household, educator, and administrator perspectives from being combined into a misleading overall average.

---

### **Expected Insights & Outcomes**
By the end of this study, you will possess the data to:

- **Validate** whether perceived content relevance is associated with sustained usage and course completion.
- **Validate** whether clear progress visibility and timely feedback reduce uncertainty and support continued learning.
- **Validate** whether adaptive learning tools improve engagement only when learners understand and trust the recommendations.
- **Validate** whether gamification and social learning influence completion differently across learner types and learning goals.
- **Validate** whether former learners are more likely to have stopped because of content, time, journey, motivation, value, trust, or competition barriers than because of one isolated feature problem.
- **Validate** whether parents, teachers, and administrators evaluate LearnSphere using materially different success criteria from learners.
- **Validate** whether potential users require stronger proof of learning outcomes, credibility, relevance, ease of use, or value before trying LearnSphere.
- **Identify** the strongest behavioural and experience-level predictors of course engagement and completion.
- **Quantify** friction across onboarding, course discovery, lessons, quizzes, progress tracking, feedback, adaptive tools, social learning, gamification, and resuming unfinished learning.
- **Diagnose** why former or inactive learners stopped using LearnSphere and distinguish recoverable users from low-probability win-back segments.
- **Compare** current learners, former learners, potential users, parents or guardians, teachers, and administrators without blending incompatible perspectives.
- **Determine** whether AI-powered learning tools, progress tracking, social learning, and gamification are noticed, trusted, valued, and linked to continued use.
- **Prioritise** the next product-release improvements using MaxDiff if LearnSphere supplies a defined set of candidate features.
- **Decide** which learner-experience problems should receive priority to improve engagement and course completion.
- **Decide** whether the next release should focus more heavily on content relevance, learning design, feedback and progress visibility, adaptive learning, social features, gamification, or journey friction.
- **Decide** which inactive learners are realistically recoverable and what intervention could bring them back.
- **Decide** what evidence and capabilities LearnSphere must strengthen before expanding into certifications or institutional partnerships.

**KPIs to report:** Active-learning frequency, course-start-to-completion behaviour, completion barriers, learner-experience satisfaction, content relevance, ease of navigation, perceived learning progress, feedback usefulness, adaptive-tool usefulness and trust, social-learning value, gamification contribution, likelihood to continue, likelihood to return, likelihood to recommend, NPS, primary churn reasons, alternative-platform usage, win-back potential, potential-user trial requirements, stakeholder-specific success criteria, and prioritised improvement utilities where MaxDiff is included.

---

### **Methodology** [See why](hercules://explain?topic=Methodology)
We will deploy an **approximately 22-question main-path survey taking 8-12 minutes** on the **SuperJ mobile application and the web** to **500** verified Indian respondents. The survey will use a linear modular design with role-based routing rather than stimulus cells.

The recommended sample is large enough to provide a directional overall read with approximately 5% margin-of-error-style precision at a 95% confidence level under simple random-sample assumptions. The sample is intended for strategic diagnosis and subgroup comparison; stakeholder-role findings should be interpreted directionally unless larger role-specific quotas are commissioned.

The questionnaire will combine fully labelled 5-point scales, behavioural frequency measures, forced-choice prioritisation where appropriate, targeted open-ended probes, NPS with reason questions, and role-specific routing. If a defined list of five or more candidate improvements is supplied, MaxDiff will be added as a prioritisation module rather than a stimulus-cell test.

**Data Collection Approach:** SuperJ mobile application and web panel, with audience targeting enforced before survey start. Age, gender, city, and NCCS will not be recollected in the questionnaire.

**Quality Controls:** Embedded attention checks, speeder removal, straight-liner detection, randomised non-ordered lists, open-ended gibberish filtering, termination logic for ineligible respondents, and separate reporting by LearnSphere relationship and stakeholder role.

---

### **Target Audience** [See why](hercules://explain?topic=Target+Audience)
The target audience will include verified Indian adults who can provide relevant evidence about LearnSphere or comparable digital-learning experiences. The sample will deliberately separate current learners, former or inactive learners, potential users, parents or guardians, teachers or instructors, and academic administrators. This structure reflects the approved framework: learners provide primary experience and completion evidence, while other stakeholders answer role-specific questions rather than being combined into a single learner satisfaction score.

**Total Sample Size:** 500 respondents

**Geographic Focus:** Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, and Pune. The four-city spread provides focused coverage across major Indian digital-learning markets without scattering the sample across too many locations.

**Demographics:**

- **Gender:** 50% male / 50% female.
- **Age Range:** 18-24, 24-35, and 35-45. The proposed distribution is 200 respondents aged 18-24, 180 aged 24-35, and 120 aged 35-45.
- **Socioeconomic Class:** NCCS A1, A2, B1, and B2, with the proposed split of A1 20%, A2 30%, B1 30%, and B2 20%.

**Behavioural and Stakeholder Filters:**

- 40% current LearnSphere learners with recent platform activity.
- 20% former or inactive LearnSphere learners who stopped using the platform or did not complete a course.
- 20% potential users who fit a relevant learning need but do not currently use LearnSphere.
- 10% parents or guardians who influence a learner’s education decision.
- 10% teachers, instructors, or academic administrators involved in learning delivery, monitoring, curriculum, or institutional decisions.

**Screening Criteria:** Respondents must be aged 18 or above, reside in India, confirm their relevant stakeholder role, and demonstrate sufficient familiarity with LearnSphere or comparable digital learning to answer the routed module. Current and former learners must report recent or past platform use. Potential users must have a relevant learning need and experience with at least one alternative learning route. Parents, teachers, instructors, and administrators must have direct influence over or professional involvement in learning decisions, delivery, monitoring, or implementation.

The sample splits are independent dimensions of the same 500 respondents: gender totals 500, age totals 500, and city totals 500. Stakeholder-role percentages are routing quotas and may overlap where a respondent legitimately holds more than one relevant role.

Do not generate age, gender, city, residence, NCCS, income, education, or other database-known targeting questions.
For potential users, measure learning need, alternatives, barriers, proof requirements, and trial intent without asking them to evaluate unexperienced LearnSphere features.
For former learners, use LIFECYCLE_INTENT_AND_WINBACK to capture return likelihood, recoverability, switching cost, and the intervention most likely to bring them back.
For current learners, use LIFECYCLE_INTENT_AND_WINBACK to capture continuation and return intent. For potential users, use it to capture trial intent.
Use dynamic lists only where the target preserves the source option text and order: alternatives to learning-time allocation and used formats to format usefulness.
Use compact, mobile-friendly measures and avoid long agree/disagree grids. Interleave behavioural, rating, forced-choice, and open-ended formats.
Show MaxDiff or Best-Worst Scaling only when a validated list of at least five candidate improvements is supplied; otherwise use the single improvement-priority measure and do not invent options.
Include quality controls at the specified ratio without creating additional questionnaire keys or sections.

termination_and_completion_policy.condition: Respondent fails the audience-system eligibility requirements or cannot confirm the required Indian adult audience status.
LEARNER_EXPERIENCE_ELIGIBILITY indicates no sufficient LearnSphere or comparable digital-learning experience.
A potential user reports no relevant learning need or no alternative learning-route experience.
An embedded attention, speed, straight-line, or open-ended quality control fails.
A question does not apply because the respondent has not used the relevant format, feature, platform, or learning route.
The optional MaxDiff or forced-trade-off prerequisite list contains fewer than five validated improvement options.
The respondent completes the final applicable improvement-priority and open-ended improvement responses.

rules.reason: Terminate respondents who cannot demonstrate sufficient LearnSphere or comparable digital-learning experience.
A respondent classified as a current LearnSphere learner must report recent LearnSphere activity.
Potential users must report a relevant learning need.
Potential users must report experience with at least one alternative learning route.
The declared eligibility gate fails before experience and satisfaction modules.
The respondent has completed the final applicable improvement response.

ambiguities: The exact option labels for LEARNER_EXPERIENCE_ELIGIBILITY, RELEVANT_LEARNING_NEED, ALTERNATIVE_LEARNING_USE, and RECENT_LEARNSPHERE_ACTIVITY are not supplied; the gate rules use the declared semantic labels Yes and No.
The audience-system eligibility and Indian adult audience gate is external to the supplied flow_keys and therefore is not represented as a questionnaire routing rule.
The optional MaxDiff or forced-trade-off task has no flow_key and no validated candidate list, so no routing rule is emitted for it.
Quality-control mechanisms are declared as embedded controls without flow_keys; their terminate outcome must be implemented by the quality-control layer.
Role-specific multi-role sequencing is not specified. ROLE_SPECIFIC_SUCCESS_CRITERIA is protected for any applicable stakeholder role without creating separate role-specific question keys.
validator_expectations: All question_keys must exist in generated questions.
All routing references use flow_key values only; no qIds or UUIDs are permitted.
The declared branch_blocks are the authoritative lifecycle fan-out and must not be duplicated with per-member showIf or go_to rules.
All dynamic filters must use identical option text and option order between source and target questions.
Only conditionally visible non-branch targets have display rules.
No demographic routing is present.
Current, former or inactive, and potential-user paths rejoin the shared flow at ALTERNATIVE_PLATFORMS_USED.
The lifecycle branch rejoins at NPS_RECOMMENDATION.
Every valid respondent path reaches MOST_IMPORTANT_IMPROVEMENT and then the completion rule, while ineligible paths terminate at the declared screening gates.
